subject: Playbook transfer: latency + streaming measurement checklist
messages:
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@edgeapps.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc:
Date: 2027-04-11T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: benchmark targets and initial prompt set

Hi Hannah / Marcus,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to align on scope. Quick recap from our side and the asks we'll need to move the benchmark forward: 

1) Targets we care about (for initial qualification):
   - Latency: P50 < 80ms, P95 < 250ms for 512-token responses (streaming enabled)
   - Throughput: sustained 200 requests/sec for the 1k-concurrent-user profile
   - Concurrency: allow 16 concurrent connections per client with graceful queuing
   - Streaming: needs to support incremental token delivery with time-to-first-byte (TTFB) < 35ms

2) Measurement definitions we want to follow (please confirm):
   - Cold vs warm KV cache: measure both (cold = new session, warm = KV primed with previous context)
   - Streaming latency: report TTFB and time-to-last-token (TTLT) separately
   - Retry/fallback behavior: track any fallback to smaller model variants and surface counts

3) Prompt set: attached a small seed set (edgeapps_seed_prompts_v0.json) — ~120 prompts across instructions, multi-turn, and long-context summarization. We'll hand over a 1k-prompt corpus once scope locked.

4) Reproducibility: we need an artifact package that includes the exact model version, quantization profile, kernel/compile flags, and the harness command used to generate metrics.

5) Timing: we'd like a canary run the week of Apr 18 and a broader run the week after (Apr 25). Can you confirm availability and what you need from us (VPC IPs, sample traffic patterns, auth tokens)?

Attachments: edgeapps_seed_prompts_v0.json (stub)

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Reyes
Head of ML Engineering, EdgeApps Inc
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@edgeapps.com>, Anika Bose <anika@infra-bench.co>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: benchmark targets and initial prompt set

Tom — thanks for the concise recap. Internal summary and proposed plan below.

Summary of what we heard:
- Your SLO targets: P50 < 80ms, P95 < 250ms at 512 tokens, streaming TTFB target of 35ms, target throughput 200 rps, concurrency ~16.
- You want cold/warm cache comparisons, streaming TTFB/TTL metrics, and a reproducible artifact (model + runtime config + harness).

Proposed Redwood deliverables (canary -> scale):
1) Measurement spec (attached measurement_spec_v1.xlsx): definitive definitions for P50/P95, TTFB, TTLT, how we handle retries and backpressure, and the warm/cold protocol.
2) Eval harness instructions (attached eval_harness_instructions.md): step-by-step commands to run the harness locally and in your VPC, with required config fields.
3) A small canary run (1–2 hours) to validate latency & streaming behavior, then a 4-hour scale run for throughput curves.
4) Reproducibility bundle: we will publish a run manifest (model hash, quant profile, kernel flags, runner config) to the shared Drive link.

What we need from EdgeApps:
- Full prompt corpus (1k prompts) or a link to S3/GDrive containing it.
- Preferred model/variant for qualification (if none, we'll use our default recommended model for your latency target).
- Expected sequence length distribution (we'll use the 512 token target by default but please confirm percentiles).
- Network info for a VPC test or test token for hosted runs.

Schedule proposal:
- Canary: Apr 19 10:00–12:00 PST (Redwood infra team on standby)
- Scale run: Apr 20 09:00–13:00 PST (contingent on canary results)

We can cover the initial artifact preparation and push the manifest to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleDriveLink

I've CC'd Marcus to coordinate the run (he'll own execution) and Grace for measurement QA.

Attachments: measurement_spec_v1.xlsx, eval_harness_instructions.md

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Anika Bose <anika@infra-bench.co>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@edgeapps.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-12T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: benchmark targets and initial prompt set

Thanks — adding a few notes from the harness/vendor perspective. Happy to run the canary and provide the reproducibility package.

Key clarifications on measurement (we'll follow Hannah's spec but calling out details):
- Streaming latency: we differentiate TTFB (first token emitted) and TTLT (final token). Our client will timestamp at request-send, first-token-received, and final-token-received.
- Bandwidth jitter: for streaming tests we will inject realistic network jitter (p50/p95) per your sequence distribution unless you ask for idealized LAN runs.
- Warm vs cold: cold = new session + empty KV, warm = KV primed with 2 previous turns. We'll run both and report side-by-side.
- Model fallbacks: our harness flags any model swap/backfill; we treat a fallback to a smaller variant as a failed SLO point unless explicitly allowed.

Attached: bench_runner_config.yml (sample runner config).

Availability for canary: Apr 19 10:00–14:00 PST (we can run multiple iterations in that window).

Reproducibility checklist we'll deliver with results:
- harness command & git commit ID
- model/version hash + quant profile used
- exact runner config (bench_runner_config.yml)
- raw per-request logs (timestamped) + aggregated metrics

One ask: please share the final 1k prompt corpus and a representative token-length histogram (percentiles) so we can generate load that mirrors production.

Thanks,
Anika Bose
Lead Benchmark Engineer — InfraBench (external vendor)
Attachment: bench_runner_config.yml

2) Please drop the 1k prompt corpus at the Drive link or S3 by EOD Apr 15 and include the token-length histogram.
3) If you have a preferred model variant name (e.g., redwood/gpt-7b-ops-v2), list it; otherwise we'll use our default latency-optimized build for the canary.
4) We'll publish the reproducibility bundle to the Drive folder and a run manifest to the Redwood run page: https://app.redwood.ai/run/rdw-2391-canary

Marcus — please own the canary execution and post a short run plan to the Drive folder by EOD Apr 14. Grace — please prepare the measurement QA checklist (mapping of raw logs -> P50/P95/TTFB).

Thanks all — looking forward to the runs.

Hannah
